Subject: Post-call: POC success gates & evaluation approach (shadow vs offline)

Hi Alice / Charlie —

Thanks again for a productive discovery call earlier. Quick recap and a proposed lean POC approach so we can get a fast answer on fit and cost/latency risk. I attached a one-page POC charter and an initial evaluation rubric for your review.

Recap (from our call)
- Primary use-case: triage + categorization of inbound clinical intake forms (~500/day).
- Key constraints: latency target 200–400ms p95, no PHI persisted outside your VPC for the pilot.
- Success criteria you mentioned: >=92% high/low triage agreement with clinical reviewers; <0.5% critical-misclassification rate; stable infra at target concurrency.

Proposed POC structure (two parallel tracks)
1) Offline baseline (2 weeks) — run a withheld dataset through candidate models to validate precision/recall and edge-case coverage. Owners: HelioCare data team + Redwood research.
2) Shadow / online observation (1 week) — run model in shadow in your environment against live traffic (read-only) to measure real-distribution metrics, latency, and false-positive profile. Owners: HelioCare infra + Redwood SRE.

Evaluation plan highlights
- Primary metrics: recall on urgent classes, precision on triage labels, inference p95 latency, operator escalation rate.
- Grading: pass/fail gates mapped in attached eval-rubric-v1.xlsx. We recommend requiring both offline OK and shadow OK for an automatic rollout.

Next steps / asks
- Alice: confirm we can get the 2-week anonymized dataset by Aug 30.
- Charlie: confirm a staging endpoint and IAM access for shadowing (RBAC token) by Sep 3.
- Internal: I'll loop in Karthik and Marissa to scope ownership and runbook details.

Attachments: POC-charter-draft.pdf, eval-rubric-v1.xlsx

Thanks —
Ben Carter

Ben / Marissa / HelioCare —

Thanks for the clear asks. Below is a pragmatic plan that respects HelioCare's compliance constraints and gives meaningful signals quickly.

Proposed plan (detailed)
- Offline baseline (2 weeks) — deliverables:
  - HelioCare supplies a de-identified CSV (schema example in Drive link). We expect a sample size of ~3k labeled examples across priority classes. Tokenization note: we'll run Redwood's preprocessing and share a token-length distribution report.
  - Redwood returns: precision/recall by class, confusion matrix, top 30 error examples, and recommended prompt engineering changes.
  - Owner: Redwood Research (Karthik) + HelioCare Data (Alice).

- Shadowing (1 week) — privacy-preserving options:
  1) Remote inference inside HelioCare VPC (preferred): Redwood ships a lightweight inference container that runs inside their network. Outputs are logged locally and a summary telemetry export (no payload) is sent to Redwood for analysis. Requires RBAC token + ephemeral keys.
  2) Replay via sanitized replica stream: HelioCare produces a redacted replay stream to a staging endpoint in their account. Redwood consumes replicas for shadow predictions (no writeback).

- Grading policy and soft-fail behavior:
  - Primary gate: offline checklist (>=92% agreement on urgent classes).
  - Secondary gate: shadow pass (latency and operational safety).
  - Soft-fail: if offline metric misses gate by <2% and shadow latency & operator burden are acceptable, we propose a conditional pass: escalate to a 1-week co-pilot review where flagged items are routed to clinicians and a manual adjudication workflow is used. This must be agreed by HelioCare clinical lead.

Runbook deliverables I will produce today:
- anonymization checklist (attach: shadow-runbook.md)
- minimal infra diagram + steps for container-based remote inference
- recommended operator flow for manual review and logging hooks (append to eval-rubric-v1.xlsx)

Next steps
- Ben: confirm timeline with HelioCare (dataset handoff by Aug 30, staging/container access by Sep 3).
- Alice: confirm which of the two shadowing options you prefer.
- Marissa: can you estimate SRE / infra time for packaging the container and verifying telemetry export? 2–3 engineer-days is my ballpark.

I'll attach the runbook and a short checklist in the next mail.

— Karthik
